sections.h2: Where is Windsor, Colorado, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Windsor is a home rule town in Northern Colorado that sits in two counties, Weld and Larimer. It was platted in 1882 and incorporated on April 2, 1890, according to Wikipedia's Windsor entry, which also gives the town an elevation of 4,797 feet and a total area of about 26 square miles.

The older core runs east and west along State Highway 392, which doubles as Main Street. The BNSF line sits just north of it, and the original street grid stretches roughly six blocks north and south of Main. The Cache la Poudre River crosses the western and southern sides of town, and several former gravel pits along it now hold lakes with houses and a golf course on their banks.

Newer growth has pushed west toward Interstate 25. In the 1990s the town limits were extended west into Larimer County, and the incorporated area west of the interstate now touches Loveland. That split matters for a seller, because a house on the Larimer side is recorded and taxed through different county offices than a house on the Weld side.

  • ZIP codes for the town: 80528, 80550 and 80551
  • Main commercial street: State Highway 392
  • Water features: Windsor Lake, the Cache la Poudre River and former gravel-pit lakes
  • Trail link: the Poudre Trail connects Windsor with Greeley

Windsor's population rose from 4,277 in 1980 to 32,716 at the 2020 census, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 43,840. The table below lists the counts Wikipedia reproduces from the decennial census.

The 2020 census counted 11,807 households and 12,846 housing units in town, with 8.1% of the units vacant. About 65.9% of households were married-couple households, and the median age was 38.2 years. Those figures describe a family-oriented suburb, and they help explain why so much of the housing stock is relatively recent.

Fast growth also means several subdivisions were built in waves, so two houses can differ widely in the age of the roof, siding and furnace.

sections.h2: What is Windsor's history and where do people work?
sections.html:
Windsor grew up around wheat, irrigation and the railroad, then around sugar beets. A flour mill came first, and in 1903 a beet sugar factory was built in town. Great Western Sugar anchored the local economy until the Windsor factory closed in the mid-1960s.

Kodak opened a manufacturing plant as the sugar factory closed, and later in the 1980s Metal Container Corporation opened a can factory. Today the town's own business pages point newcomers to a Chamber of Commerce and a Downtown Development Authority, and the town requires a business license for every new business.

For a seller, the job mix matters less than the commute. Windsor sits between Fort Collins and Greeley, with Loveland close on the west, so buyers and renters often work in one of those cities and live here for the lot size or the newer construction.

sections.h2: Which Windsor weather events affect a house sale?
sections.html:
Hail and tornadoes are the two risks that come up most. Wikipedia reports that Windsor typically sees between 6 and 12 hail days a year, and that the area where Colorado, Nebraska and Wyoming meet receives more hail than any other location in the United States.

On May 22, 2008, a tornado struck Windsor and parts of Weld and Larimer counties. The National Weather Service surveys documented pockets of EF3 damage and wind estimates up to 165 mph, along with hail up to baseball size. The storm caused $193.5 million in damage from about 24,000 auto and homeowner claims, and it damaged the Windsor Milling and Elevator Company building, which is on the National Register of Historic Places.

  • A roof with old hail damage is a likely item for a buyer's inspector to flag.
  • Insurance claim history can come up when a buyer's lender or insurer reviews the house.
  • Wide daily temperature swings, which can top 50 degrees Fahrenheit in spring and fall, are hard on exterior paint, sealant and concrete flatwork.

A cash buyer purchases the house as it stands, so a hail-worn roof does not have to be replaced before closing. That is one reason owners with storm damage ask about it.

Most of Windsor is in the Weld RE-4 School District. Wikipedia lists these RE-4 schools in town: Windsor High School, Windsor Middle School, Grandview Elementary, Hollister Lake Elementary, Mountain View Elementary, Orchard Hill Elementary, Skyview Elementary, Tozer Primary School, and the charter schools American Legacy Academy, Windsor Charter Elementary and Windsor Charter Middle and High.

Buyers often ask which school a street feeds, and a listing agent or the district can answer that. A seller who goes the cash route skips that conversation entirely.

sections.h2: What does the Town of Windsor require for repairs and permits?
sections.html:
Windsor runs its own building permit desk at 200 N. 11th Street. The town's building permit page says the desk is open to the public Monday through Thursday, with online services on Fridays.

Under that page, new building plans are reviewed under the 2024 I-Codes, effective January 1, 2026, and the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code takes effect in Windsor on July 1, 2026. The town also publishes homeowner handouts for re-roofs, decks, basement finishes, patio covers and pools.

The town's Homeowners Resource Center also carries HOA information and a wildfire code map. Owners are encouraged to check the map and to ask their insurer about any wildfire-related requirements. If you have open permits or unfinished work, sort that out with the permit technician before a buyer's inspector finds it.

sections.h2: Which county office handles a Windsor sale?
sections.html:
That depends on which side of the county line the house sits. For a Weld County address, deeds are recorded by the Weld County Clerk and Recorder at 1250 H Street in Greeley, and the office charges $43.00 to record a letter or legal size document regardless of page count. Colorado's state documentary fee is $.01 per $100 of sale price when the price is over $500, per the county's fee page.

On a $400,000 sale that fee works out to $40.00. We did not confirm Larimer County's recording office details for this page, so owners west of I-25 should ask their title company which county applies.

sections.h2: How are property taxes handled when a Windsor house sells?
sections.html:
For Weld County parcels, the Treasurer says property taxes are due January 1 for the previous year and can be paid in two equal installments or one full payment. The 2026 dates posted by the county are February 28 for the first half, June 15 for the second half and April 30 for full payment.

Late payments carry interest that starts at 1% and climbs month by month. The Treasurer also offers a Certificate of Taxes Due request form, which title companies use to confirm that nothing is owed before closing. See the county treasurer's tax information page for the full schedule.

Because tax notices go to the owner of record, a seller who has moved out should confirm the mailing address on file so a bill is not missed during a sale.

sections.h2: What choices does a Windsor seller have?
sections.html:
A Windsor owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer. Each has a different timeline, and the right pick depends on the house's condition and how soon you need to close.

  • Listing with an agent: showings, buyer financing and appraisal, and repairs the buyer's inspector requests.
  • Selling it yourself: you handle marketing, contracts and disclosures, and you still need a title company.
  • Cash offer: the buyer purchases as-is, and closing runs through a title company on a date that suits you.

Owners who inherited a Windsor house, are behind on payments, have tenants in place, or are sitting on hail or storm damage tend to look at the third option. If that sounds like you, send the address through the form on this page for a written cash offer with no obligation.

faqs.q: Is Windsor, CO in Weld County or Larimer County?
faqs.a: Both. Windsor is a home rule municipality that lies in Weld and Larimer counties,; the town limits were extended west into Larimer County in the 1990s.

faqs.q: How many people live in Windsor, Colorado?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau counted 32,716 residents in 2020 and estimates 43,840 for 2025.

faqs.q: Does Windsor require a contractor license for repairs before I sell?
faqs.a: No. The Town of Windsor says no contractor license is required for work inside the Town, although electrical and plumbing contractors must hold a state license, and most projects still need a building permit.

faqs.q: When are Weld County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due January 1 for the previous year. For 2026 the county lists February 28 for the first half, June 15 for the second half and April 30 for a single full payment.

faqs.q: Can I sell a hail-damaged house in Windsor without replacing the roof?
faqs.a: Yes, if the buyer agrees to take it as it is. A cash buyer purchases without requiring roof replacement first, while a financed buyer's lender or insurer may ask for repairs.
